issues: A few phrases imply formalised governance mechanisms (eg ‘integration indicators’, ‘climate checks’) beyond what is evidenced; these should be reframed to the narrower evidenced facts.
Some effectiveness-signalling language (‘reflects’, ‘supported by’) could be interpreted as over-claiming governance strength rather than describing processes and evidence-backed activities.
unsupported_claims: “Eurolux Universal Bank AG organises climate-related governance across the Board of Directors, the ESG & Sustainability Committee and executive management.” (The existence of the ESG & Sustainability Committee is evidenced, but a formal governance mandate/role description is not; the draft later notes no charter/ToR, but the opening sentence still reads like a formalised governance design statement.)

“Board and committee oversight of climate-related risks and opportunities is reflected in documented climate-related decisions in 2024.” (Decisions are evidenced, but the phrasing implies those decisions, by themselves, demonstrate effective oversight; this should be framed more neutrally as ‘illustrated by’ or ‘includes’.)

“Skills and incentives are supported by the Board’s climate expertise profile…” (The expertise percentage and remuneration metrics are evidenced; ‘supported by’ is slightly causal/assurance-like and could be tightened.)
material_unsupported_claims: “integration indicators with the enterprise risk management (ERM) framework” / “six were flagged as integrated into the ERM framework.” (The ERM integration flag/count is evidenced, but the draft implies a defined ‘indicator’ system; reframe to the evidenced fact that the register flags ERM integration for 6 of 8 risks, without implying a formal indicator framework.)

“The Bank has climate checks for major transactions.” (Evidence supports that climate checks are applied for major transactions, but it does not evidence a formal policy/mandatory control; reframe to avoid implying a formalised bank-wide control requirement.)

ifrs_required_but_missing_in_data.item: Formal climate-specific Board/committee mandate or terms of reference
Formal escalation thresholds / trigger-based escalation mechanics for climate risks
Quantified Board-level trade-offs between climate and other objectives
Formal process for assessing adequacy of Board climate skills and competencies

minor_wording_to_tighten: Use of “reflects” in relation to agenda coverage and semi-annual reporting (“reflects the Board’s oversight…”)—tighten to “supports” / “is consistent with” / “includes” to avoid over-claiming effectiveness.
“The ESG & Sustainability Committee… provides a forum for more detailed consideration…”—acceptable, but could be tightened to avoid implying a formal remit beyond evidenced activity.
Risk-register mitigation action examples: ensure they are clearly described as actions recorded in the register (as drafted) and avoid implying they are fully implemented bank-wide controls.
correctly_disclosed_evidence_boundaries: “The Bank’s governance information… does not include a separate climate-specific committee charter or terms of reference.”
“The Bank’s climate-related Board decisions do not describe specific quantified trade-offs…”
“The Bank does not currently disclose formal escalation thresholds or trigger-based escalation mechanics for climate-related risks.”
“The Bank does not currently disclose a formal Board skills adequacy assessment process specific to climate-related oversight.”
Assurance boundary: limited assurance by EY under ISAE 3000 over Scope 1 and Scope 2 only; financed emissions and other Scope 3 categories are outside scope.
